name: @cloudsforge/foresight
description: Forge Foresight: a parimutuel prediction market native to Hearth. The stake and the payout are the contract's; this service orchestrates the lifecycle, proposes questions for a person to approve, and mirrors the chain.

scripts._test: --test-concurrency=1 is required, not a preference: every database test file truncates this service's tables between cases, and node:test runs FILES in parallel by default. A TRUNCATE takes an AccessExclusiveLock, so one file's reset deadlocks against another file's inserts (40P01). Cases within a file already run in order.
scripts._compile:contracts: Regenerates the COMMITTED artefact src/contracts/generated.ts. CI reruns it and fails on any diff, which is what stops the bytecode this service deploys drifting from the source a reviewer read. The solc version is EXACT-pinned for exactly that reason.

_localDependencies: Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:'. A 'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of
these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a publishConfig that points main/types at dist/.
Packing therefore installs a package whose exports resolve to a dist/ that has not been built,
while its 'main' in the working tree still says src/index.ts. 'link:' symlinks the checkout in
place, so the working-tree manifest is the one that is read and the package keeps using its own
@cloudsforge/contracts-chain is EXACT-PINNED, never caret-ranged. This service and custody must
agree byte-for-byte about a chain id: a skew there is not a 500, it is a market contract bound
to the wrong network holding stakes nobody can claim.
There is no chain library in the RUNTIME dependencies — no ethers, no viem. This service builds
ONE EVM transaction shape (a legacy zero-value contract creation) and hands it to custody as a
JSON object; custody is the only place a private key exists and therefore the only place a
serialiser is needed. What is left is keccak256, for EIP-55, for the transaction id and for the
CREATE address derivation, and that is a permutation table rather than a dependency on the one
path where a wrong answer deploys a market to an address nobody can find.
tsx is a runtime dependency because the unpublished packages resolve to their TypeScript
sources. On publish their publishConfig points at dist/, tsx moves to devDependencies, and the
_devDependencies: solc is EXACT-pinned, because `contracts` in CI recompiles src/contracts/ForesightMarket.sol
and diffs the committed artefact. A caret range would make that job produce different bytes on
a different day and the diff would be noise rather than signal.
@ethereumjs/evm is the contract test harness and it is ONE dependency doing one job: execute
the compiled bytecode. The alternatives were worse. Hardhat and Foundry each bring a toolchain
and a second build system into a repository whose whole compile step is 90 lines of solc; a
real Hearth node cannot be required by CI, and a suite that skips when a node is absent proves
nothing on the one machine that matters. The invariants below — that a pool sums exactly, that
a second claim reverts, that resolution before close reverts — are statements about EXECUTED
bytecode, and there is no way to make them without an EVM.
